title: 2-on-1 Fast Break
description: Two attackers race a lone defender up the court and must make the defender commit before finishing, teaching the basic decision of a numbers advantage.

content.objective: Attack at pace with two players against one defender, force the defender to pick a player, and finish or pass to the open teammate.
content.setup: Two lines of attackers on the baseline, a defender waiting near the free-throw line at the far end. The middle attacker starts with the ball. When the play ends, the defender becomes an attacker in the next round.
content.organization: Three lines: two attacking lines at one baseline and a defending line at the other end. Attackers who finish become the defenders on the way back.
instructions: Attackers sprint up the court, ball handler in the middle, the second attacker in a lane about four metres wide of the ball handler.
The ball handler attacks the defender at full speed until the defender has to step to the ball.
If the defender stays with the ball handler, pass to the lane runner for a layup; if the defender stops the passing lane, the ball handler finishes.
The defender tries to stop the ball first and recover to the second attacker.
After the shot, the attackers stay to rebound and the defender starts the next attack with the second pair.
coachingPoints: Keep the lanes wide: attackers stretch the defender before the pass is needed.
Ball handler attacks the defender's front foot; do not stop and wait.
Pass early enough for the receiver to finish without breaking stride.
Defender: sprint back, get in the lane, then stop the ball first.
commonMistakes: Both attackers run close together, so one defender covers both.
Ball handler picks up the dribble too early.
Passing after the defender has already recovered.
content.safety: Keep the finishing lanes clear of other lines. Attackers and defender finish in a balanced stop, never running into the stanchion.
progressions: Add a second defender that trails so it becomes 2-on-1, then 2-on-2 recovery.
regressions: Walk through at half speed with the defender standing still in the key.
variations: Award two points for a layup on a pass and one point for an unassisted finish.
